chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 67 — Noah’s Preservation and the Fiery Waters
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for this Noahic unit within the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all thirteen verses: God's promise to preserve Noah and his seed, the fiery valley where corrupting angels are confined, the changing hot waters used by rulers for bodily healing, and Michael's declaration that those same waters become testimony and judgment. The witness's difficult sequence connecting sulfurous metal, angelic punishment, therapeutic springs and their final transformation into fire is retained without supplying a modern physical explanation. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: In those days the word of God came to me and said, ‘Noah, behold, your portion has come up before Me—a portion without reproach, a portion of love and uprightness.’
verses.study: Noah's preservation begins with a moral portion known before God. Love and uprightness, not mere survival instinct, distinguish him from the condemned world.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:8–9 — Noah finds favor and is called righteous
Psalm 16:5 — the LORD Himself secures the faithful person's portion

verses.text: ‘Now the angels are making a wooden structure. When they have gone out to that task, I will place My hand upon it and preserve it. From it the seed of life will come, and a change will enter so that the dry ground will not remain empty.’
verses.study: The wooden vessel becomes an instrument held beneath God's own preserving hand. Its purpose is continuity: life will emerge after the world-changing flood.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:14–22 — the ark is built to preserve life
1 Peter 3:20 — a few are safely carried through water

verses.text: ‘I will establish your seed before Me forever and ever. I will scatter those who dwell with you over the face of the dry ground; it will be blessed and multiplied upon the earth in the name of the Lord.’
verses.study: Preservation expands into blessing and multiplication. Noah's household is not kept for isolation but for renewed life across the earth.
crossReferences: Genesis 9:1, 7 — Noah's family is blessed to multiply and fill the earth
Isaiah 54:9–10 — the Noahic promise supports enduring covenant mercy

verses.text: ‘Those angels who revealed unrighteousness will be shut within that burning valley which my grandfather Enoch showed me earlier in the west, near the mountains of gold, silver, iron, molten metal and tin.’
verses.study: The corrupting angels are confined near the very metals associated with forbidden disclosure. Noah links the place back to Enoch's earlier journey, preserving continuity between the visions.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 10:11–14 — the rebellious Watchers are bound until judgment
2 Peter 2:4 — sinning angels are confined for judgment

verses.text: I saw that valley, and there was a great convulsion within it, and the waters were convulsed.
verses.study: The valley's instability becomes visible in land and water alike. The scene prepares the union of fiery material, sulfurous odor and judgment below.
crossReferences: Psalm 46:3 — waters roar and mountains tremble
Revelation 16:18–20 — an unmatched shaking accompanies final judgment

verses.text: When all this took place, from that fiery molten metal and from the convulsion that shook them in that place a smell of sulfur arose and mingled with those waters. That valley belonging to the angels who led people astray burns beneath that ground.
verses.study: The witness combines metal, sulfur, water and subterranean fire in an ancient judgment landscape. Its point is the corrupting angels' confinement, not a modern account of geothermal chemistry.
crossReferences: Genesis 19:24 — sulfur and fire accompany judgment
Revelation 19:20 — burning sulfur marks the defeat of deceiving powers

verses.text: Through its valleys rivers of fire come out, where those angels who led the inhabitants of the dry ground astray are judged.
verses.study: The rivers emerge from the place of the deceivers' judgment. Their former influence over the earth ends in a sentence located beneath it.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:10 — a river of fire flows from the heavenly court
Jude 6 — rebellious angels are kept for the judgment of the great day

verses.text: In those days those waters will serve the kings, the mighty, the exalted, and those who dwell upon the dry ground for the healing of soul and body, but also for the judgment of the spirit. Desire will fill their spirits so that their bodies may be judged, because they denied the Lord of Spirits. They see their judgment every day, yet they do not believe in His name.
verses.study: The rulers treat the waters as healing while refusing the judgment they signify. Bodily relief cannot cure a spirit filled with desire and denial.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 8:11–15 — superficial healing cannot remove deep judgment
John 5:39–40 — people can encounter testimony yet refuse to come for true life

verses.text: As the heat of their bodies becomes great, so a corresponding change will come upon their spirits forever and ever; for no one speaks an empty word before the Lord of Spirits.
verses.study: Physical heat anticipates a lasting spiritual transformation. The final clause anchors the sentence in the truthfulness of God's court, where no empty defense can stand.
crossReferences: Matthew 12:36 — every empty word comes under judgment
Hebrews 4:13 — nothing is hidden before the One to whom account is owed

verses.text: For judgment will come upon them because they trusted in the desire of their bodies and denied the Spirit of the Lord.
verses.study: The rulers' fault is not embodiment itself but trust placed in bodily desire against God's Spirit. Their chosen allegiance becomes the ground of judgment.
crossReferences: Romans 8:5–8 — the mind set on the flesh resists God
Galatians 6:7–8 — sowing to bodily corruption yields corruption

verses.text: Those waters themselves will undergo a change in those days. When those angels are judged, the heat of the springs of water will change; and when the angels ascend, that spring water will change and become cold.
verses.study: The waters' temperature is tied within the vision to the angels' judicial state. Change in the springs witnesses that the unseen judgment has consequences in the visible place.
crossReferences: Exodus 15:23–25 — water is changed under divine direction
Revelation 8:10–11 — waters become signs of heavenly judgment

verses.text: I heard holy Michael answer and say, ‘This judgment by which the angels are judged is a testimony against the kings, the mighty, and those who possess the dry ground.’
verses.study: Angelic punishment warns earthly rulers that elevated status does not prevent accountability. The unseen sentence becomes testimony to those still abusing visible authority.
crossReferences: Isaiah 24:21 — heavenly powers and earthly kings are judged together
2 Peter 2:4–6 — judgments on angels and ancient peoples become warnings

verses.text: ‘For these waters of judgment serve for the healing of the angels and for the death of their bodies. They will neither see nor understand that the waters will change and become a fire that burns forever.’
verses.study: The closing paradox joins apparent healing to death and water to fire. Failure to understand the sign leaves the condemned unprepared for its final transformation.
crossReferences: Isaiah 66:24 — judgment is portrayed with unquenched fire
Revelation 20:10 — deceiving powers meet enduring fiery judgment

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 67 begins with covenant preservation. Noah's portion is love and uprightness, the wooden vessel is placed under God's hand, and his seed is established to repopulate the dry ground.

The vision then returns to the angels who disclosed unrighteousness. They are confined in a western valley where metals, sulfur, disturbed waters and subterranean fire form a severe judgment landscape.
Kings use the waters for healing while refusing their testimony. Their deeper disease is spiritual: bodily desire becomes the object of trust, while the Spirit of the Lord is denied.

Michael interprets angelic judgment as a warning to earthly power. The waters' changing character exposes the difference between temporary bodily relief and the lasting fire awaiting unrepentant deception.

crossReferences: Genesis 6:14–22 — the ark preserving the seed of life
Genesis 9:1, 7 — Noah's seed blessed and multiplied
Isaiah 24:21 — heavenly and earthly powers judged
2 Peter 2:4–6 — earlier judgments as testimony
Revelation 20:10 — enduring judgment of deceiving powers
